corrections.finding: Section Var 6–7 started at 172 s. corrections.finding: First publication rested on Stuart’s discography alone; the strings-entry note had no period source for the basses’ fugue.

checks.source: MEAS: item metadata read (CHARM, matrix AR_8464-4, catalogue 1153); cached MP3 MD5 5979a0509d58… equals the manifest; 253.61 s; complete movement (tenor from about 1.4 s to a final low G on his own at about 250 s). Pitch: tune centred on G4 about 392 Hz; horn F5/E5 at the entry measure 698–705 Hz and 658–661 Hz, so about A = 440 within +10 cents.
checks.identity: EXT: Stuart session 0288 and CHARM METS_AK_1151 as for the Elegy. Take 4 of 8464; the dossier’s 8 Oct 1944 date is an inference from the re-made-sides statement and says so (an early-November 1944 Britten postcard about the new Serenade takes, quoted in a Gramophone feature, fits an October remake; that page was not opened).
checks.notes: EXT: LA Phil note by Herbert Glass verified: no marking other than come un lamento, constant mezza voce following Pears; Palmer quotations (fugally impelled funeral procession; unregardingly, impassively independent; close enough to strike mortal terror; horn hysteria; makes off; disembodied wail and whine of the singer); premiere 15 Oct 1943 with Walter Goehr (Wigmore Hall from Wikipedia); Britten tribute to Brain (met summer 1942; His help was invaluable in writing the work). Sun Valley note: RAF Orchestra, radio scores 1942. Cooke: six-bar theme, tenor begins and ends alone, horn at From Brig o’ Dread with the cellos’ and basses’ first-entry music. Nine stanzas confirmed. MEAS: bass band enters at about 28.7 s; horn F5→E5 at about 138 s, level jump at 139.8 s. Basses are still sounding in the first part of the ninth stanza (to about 233 s); the tenor is alone at the end, so the cue wording (ends alone) stands as Cooke’s. Six notes for 253.6 s (limit 7). Voice rules checked. Not an aural review.
